title: Customer Weatherboard: Snapshot and Minimal Patches
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operational synthesis of recent customer signals (last 6 weeks) focused on small, high-leverage fixes we can ship quickly. Think of this as a weatherboard: high-level conditions, gusts (urgent complaints), and recommended tarps/minimal patches to keep customers dry while we scope larger remedies.

Context and scope:
- Sources: CS tickets, renewals calls, Solutions Eng notes, three NPS follow-ups (mid-September to early October), and two field calls from enterprise pilots.
- Coverage: Hosted API + Console ergonomics + Dedicated capacity onboarding. Private deployments largely quiet this cycle.
- Goal: produce 6 candidate minimal patches (<= 2 sprint effort each) with owner suggestions and expected impact.

Topline summary (headline conditions):
- Stable base satisfaction but repeated small frictions are creating outsized operational load on CS and SRE.
- Biggest recurring themes: opaque quota/limit errors, confusing model-fallback behavior, and difficulty diagnosing latency/cost spikes from the Console.
- Several customers report engineering teams building fragile heuristics around tokenization and chunking to avoid costly re-runs; this is a sign we should prioritize clearer batching and token-cost visibility.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We keep hitting a 429-like limit but it shows as 'internal'. Hard to tell what to change." (mid-market analytics platform)
- "Model fallback is great, but our SLA wants to prefer latency over cost — the UI hides that setting in an unexpected place." (enterprise fintech pilot)
- "We saw a 3x token bill overnight after a rollout. The console graphs didn't help because they aggregate across routes." (startup with heavy chat usage)

Signal breakdown (quick clusters):
1) Error transparency (30% of signals)
   - Symptoms: customers receive ambiguous errors (rate-limited vs capacity vs auth). Ticket churn: many reopenings.
   - Root hints: current error codes are too generic; Console surface area for per-route quota is limited.
2) Model routing/fallback clarity (22%)
   - Symptoms: unexpected fallback to cheaper models without clear telemetry or route-level preference.
   - Root hints: routing policy UI and API flagging inconsistent; lack of per-request metadata in logs.
3) Cost/latency observability (25%)
   - Symptoms: bills spike post-deploys, token attribution unclear, graphs aggregate too coarsely.
   - Root hints: need finer-grain token-level attribution and anomaly alerts.
4) Batch/prefix/cache guidance (15%)
   - Symptoms: customers invent token-level batching heuristics; underutilized server-side caching.
   - Root hints: Optimize suggestions lacking in onboarding and Console recommendations.
5) Dedicated onboarding friction (8%)
   - Symptoms: initial capacity sizing uncertain, autoscale surprises during traffic bursts.

Minimal patches (ranked by expected CS time saved / engineering effort)
1) Return clear error taxonomy in API responses (ETA: 1 sprint)
   - What: Add structured error codes (quota_exceeded, capacity_constrained, auth_failure) and short human-readable hints including remediation links.
   - Why: cuts reopen rate, reduces CS hand-holding.
   - Owner: eng-platform (error surface) + docs (quicklinks).
2) Per-route quota display + export (ETA: 1 sprint)
   - What: Console pane listing quotas & recent usage per route, CSV export.
   - Why: empowers customers to self-diagnose 429s.
   - Owner: Console eng + CS for acceptance criteria.
3) Route-level routing preference toggle (latency vs cost) (ETA: 1.5 sprints)
   - What: Simple UI toggle and API param to prefer latency or prefer cost for fallback decisions; log a per-request decision bit.
   - Why: reduces surprise fallbacks for enterprise SLAs.
   - Owner: product-hosted-api + serving-runtime.
4) Token-attribution drilldown (ETA: 2 sprints)
   - What: Console time-series with per-model and per-route token counts + top contributing request signatures. Lightweight anomaly alert (email/Slack) for sudden 2x+ token change.
   - Why: prevents billing surprises and reduces billing disputes.
   - Owner: observability + console-and-tooling.
5) Quick onboarding checklist for Dedicated sizing (ETA: 1 sprint)
   - What: concise workbook + capacity calculator (spreadsheet) and a checklist for common pitfalls (burst planning, autoscale thresholds).
   - Why: reduces back-and-forth with Solutions Eng and SRE.
   - Owner: solutions-engineering-and-professional-services + infra.
6) Inline Optimize hints for common prompt patterns (ETA: 1 sprint)
   - What: Console shows 2–3 quick batching/cache suggestions when Console detects repeated prefix patterns (e.g., system messages repeated across calls).
   - Why: immediate unit cost reduction for customers who don't run deeper evals.
   - Owner: optimize + developer-experience.

Quick impact/effort matrix (qualitative):
- Highest impact / low effort: error taxonomy + per-route quota display.
- Medium impact / medium effort: routing preference toggle, token-attribution drilldown.
- Low-medium impact / low effort: Dedicated checklist, inline Optimize hints.

Acceptance criteria (for releases):
- Error taxonomy: all public endpoints return new code fields; docs page + Console link for each code. CS runbook updated.
- Per-route quota: route list shows last 7 days usage and current soft/hard limits; export passes QA.
- Routing toggle: toggles reflected in routing decisions for a test traffic pattern; logs include decision bit.

Risks and unknowns:
- Token attribution: need to ensure low-cardinality storage for request signatures to avoid cost blowup. Explore sampling strategy first.
- Routing toggle: must ensure no policy allows SLA defeats; legal/contract team to confirm on enterprise commitments.

Suggested next steps (operational):
1) Ask Console eng + Observability for 30-minute sync this week to confirm feasibility and rough effort. Tag: @Evelyn.
2) CS to prioritize a list of 6 customers to pilot error taxonomy changes (we can remove from the churn list). Tag: @Tomás.
3) Prod infra check: validate whether current logging platform can accept the per-request decision bit without ingestion cost spike. Tag: @Samir.
4) Draft quick Dedicated sizing workbook and share with two active Solutions Eng contacts for feedback.

Notes to self / whispers:
- Keep patches narrow: customers want immediate relief not big re-architects.
- This doc should be the input for a one-pager to send to Eng leads next Monday.

Open questions for discussion:
- Do we want the routing preference to be a per-customer default or per-route? (Ops tradeoff).
- What sampling rate is acceptable for token attribution traces?

Appendix: quick CS triage play (if we ship error taxonomy first)
- Update canned reply templates: map older ambiguous errors -> suggested immediate checks (API key, rate window, route quotas).
- Template for billing spike: how to pull token attribution CSV and next steps.

End.
